note: Wheels built here because no published wheel exists for the target. Filled from the build record after sls runs INTEL-CRYPTO-WHEEL-PASTE.txt; an artifact is accepted only by its sha256. proxy-tools has no published wheel at all, and every pywebview after 3.4 requires it.

wheels.openssl: 4.0.3 (static, no-module: the legacy provider is built in; prefix, openssldir and libdir /private/etc/ssl)
wheels.built_with: CPython 3.11 x86_64 native, maturin 1.15.0, rustc 1.93.1 target x86_64-apple-darwin; OpenSSL Configure darwin64-x86_64-cc no-shared no-module no-tests no-docs --prefix=/private/etc/ssl --openssldir=/private/etc/ssl --libdir=/private/etc/ssl/lib -mmacosx-version-min=14.0; sources unpacked and built at fixed paths, TMPDIR inside the build dir; RUSTFLAGS --remap-path-prefix and CFLAGS -ffile-prefix-map for the home, the runner temp dir, cargo, rustup and the build dir; SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=315532800, ZERO_AR_DATE=1, codegen-units=1, CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0, debug info stripped; wheel repacked deterministically with the cargo SBOM's paths, serial number and timestamp removed and RECORD rewritten
wheels.built_on: 2026-10-14 (native x86_64, GitHub Actions macos-15-intel runner image, macOS 15.7.9)
wheels.checks: single wheel tagged cp311-abi3-macosx_14_0_x86_64, 3818869 bytes; _rust.abi3.so x86_64 only; no libssl/libcrypto dylib; imports with the legacy provider loaded and a Fernet round-trip on this native Intel host
